security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally executes the local Codex CLI and parses newly created Codex session JSONL files to recover generated image payloads. I confirmed the hidden .codex session access and the actual external CLI invocation as the main risks; most markdown backticks, documentation URLs, device redirects, and temporary files are false positives. No prompt injection text or credential exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The workflow reads hidden Codex session rollout files from the user home directory.
remediation.suggestion: Use an official Codex image output path or session identifier when available. Until then, warn users clearly and restrict parsing to a verified session file.

remediation.issue: The session diff can include rollout files from unrelated concurrent Codex runs.
remediation.suggestion: Add a lock around the invocation or match a unique session marker before extracting image data. Fail closed if more than the expected session appears.

remediation.issue: The skill launches a local external CLI and sends user prompts and reference images through that login.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the read-only sandbox, document the data transfer path, validate timeout values, and pin the supported Codex CLI behavior.

remediation.issue: Bundled gallery images are binary assets with embedded provenance metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Publish checksums and keep source prompts or provenance notes. Strip nonessential metadata if marketplace policy requires minimal binary assets.

semantic_findings.title: External Codex CLI Execution With User Content
semantic_findings.description: The script invokes the local Codex CLI with image generation enabled and sends the user prompt through stdin. Arguments are quoted, but the workflow can transmit prompts and reference images through the user's Codex login.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The execution path is explicit: the script builds codex exec arguments and runs codex with image_generation enabled. The documentation also states that Codex reuses the logged-in ChatGPT session.

semantic_findings.title: Codex Session Log Diff Race
semantic_findings.description: The script snapshots the whole Codex sessions directory, runs Codex, then scans every new rollout file. If another Codex session writes during that window, this skill can parse a session file it did not create.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code uses a before and after diff of ~/.codex/sessions rather than a session identifier returned by Codex. The race depends on concurrent Codex activity, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Agents often need image generation without separate API setup. This skill routes prompts and reference images through a local Codex login to save generated files.
actual_capabilities: Generates images from text prompts through local Codex CLI image generation.
Edits or restyles one or more reference images using repeatable reference inputs.
Saves generated output as PNG, JPEG, or WebP after output path validation.
Extracts generated image payloads from newly created Codex rollout files.
Reports clear failure layers for missing tools, authentication issues, or missing image payloads.
limitations: Requires a local Codex CLI login with a ChatGPT plan that includes image generation.
Does not provide direct OpenAI API access, separate billing, or extra quota.
Reads local Codex session rollout files to recover the generated image payload.
Depends on Codex CLI image-generation behavior that may change across versions.

use_cases.description: Generate social graphics, posters, and concept images from concise text prompts.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Image Prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Use GPT Image 2 to create a square image of [subject] in [style]. Save it as [file name].

prompt_templates.title: Reference Restyle
prompt_templates.prompt: Use GPT Image 2 with this reference image. Keep the main composition and restyle it as [desired style].

prompt_templates.title: Multi-Reference Composition
prompt_templates.prompt: Use GPT Image 2 with these reference images. Combine the product shape, color palette, and background mood into one polished concept.

prompt_templates.title: Production Asset Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Use GPT Image 2 to create [asset type] for [audience]. Include [required text], avoid [constraints], and save the final file at [path].

output_examples.input: Use GPT Image 2 to create a product poster for a reusable water bottle in a clean studio style.
output_examples.output: A saved poster image with the requested product focus, lighting, and composition, plus the final file path.

output_examples.input: Use this logo reference and repaint it as a vintage travel badge while keeping the silhouette readable.
output_examples.output: A restyled image that preserves the logo shape and applies the requested vintage badge treatment.

output_examples.input: Use two references to create a launch graphic that combines the first image color palette with the second image layout.
output_examples.output: A composed launch graphic that follows both references and is saved in the requested image format.

best_practices: Confirm the user wants the GPT Image 2 route before invoking the local script.
Use explicit output paths and image formats so generated files are easy to find.
Warn users that prompts and reference images pass through their local Codex login.
anti_patterns: Do not substitute another image model when the user requested GPT Image 2.
Do not rewrite the user prompt unless the user asks for prompt improvement.
Do not run the workflow without checking that Codex CLI and Python are available.

faq.question: Does this skill include GPT Image 2 access?
faq.answer: No. It uses the user's existing Codex CLI login and ChatGPT image-generation entitlement.

faq.question: Can it edit an existing image?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports one or more reference images for restyling, editing, or visual composition.

faq.question: Does it call the OpenAI API directly?
faq.answer: No. It runs the local Codex CLI, which uses the user's logged-in ChatGPT session.

faq.question: Where are generated images saved?
faq.answer: The script writes the decoded image to the output path selected by the caller.

faq.question: What local files does it read?
faq.answer: It reads newly created Codex rollout files under the local .codex sessions directory.

faq.question: What tools must be installed?
faq.answer: The workflow requires the Codex CLI and Python 3 on the local PATH.
